column1: # depends on, the version it was verified at, and how.
# Several of our security properties are not ours. They are behaviours of an
# upstream project that someone read once, at one version, and then built on.
# Each was true at that version. None of them is a promise.
# A version bump is exactly the moment a vendor behaviour changes, and also the
# moment nobody re-reads the reasoning that depended on it. So the gate sits on
# the bump: this file records the version, api/internal/gatereg's test reads the
# version the tree actually pins, and a difference fails until the row has been
#   id          a stable key for the row.
#   version     the version the capability was verified at.
#   capability  what we rely on it to do. Specific enough to re-test.
#   verified    HOW it was checked - the column that makes this a record rather
#               than a wish. `unverified` is allowed and must cite a probe.
#   pin         where the tree pins the version:
#                 elsewhere:<repo path>    pinned in another repository; this
#                                          gate records it and cannot check it
#   cite        the issue or probe, required when `verified` is `unverified`.
# Do NOT edit `version` to make the gate pass. Re-verify the capability at the
# version the tree now pins, then write down what you did in `verified`.

column5: verified

column4: K-EVENTS: with eventsEnabled, a wrong password stores a LOGIN_ERROR (error invalid_user_credentials or user_not_found) whose ipAddress is the address in the X-Forwarded-For a trusted proxy (proxy-trusted-addresses) wrote and whose clientId names the client; GET /admin/realms/{realm}/events and /admin-events order by time alone, with no tie-breaker (model/jpa JpaEventQuery and JpaAdminEventQuery), so offset pages can order one millisecond's events differently and drop one between them, and take dateFrom as an inclusive epoch-millisecond floor and direction=asc, which the drain reads by instead of by offset; each event has an id; a request's events are stamped with their time before they commit and are committed before its answer completes (EventBuilder stores an error event in a transaction of its own; CloseSessionFilter commits the request's before the response is closed)

column4: The Pwned Passwords range API: GET /range/<5 hex> with Add-Padding: true answers 200 with CRLF-terminated SUFFIX:COUNT lines, each suffix 35 upper-case hex characters, padding entries carrying a count of 0; a lower-case prefix also answers 200; no API key is needed and the endpoint carries no licence or attribution requirement

column4: K-RESET: a GET of login-actions/reset-credentials with client_id and redirect_uri and no auth session runs the realm's reset flow (resetCredentialsFlow) for that client, and is refused unless resetPasswordAllowed is true (LoginActionsService.java:459); Choose User drops an unknown or disabled account and the flow goes on with no user; the flow ends with a redirect to redirect_uri carrying a code and no state; the code exchanges with no code_verifier and the answer carries no id_token, since the entry's auth session has no scope note (LoginActionsService.java:472-516, OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:146, TokenUtil.java:99-101); the access token carries the door's iss, the client's azp, typ Bearer and the account's sub under the basic default scope
column5: Exercised at 26.8.2 by TestReset_AgainstPinnedKeycloak (api/internal/identitytest): TC-992-25 (an unknown name and a codeless account get the same codeless sentence), TC-992-26 and TC-992-27 (a code reset at each door ends on reset-done), TC-992-37 (the redirect carries a code and no state; ExchangeCode finds no id_token; ExchangeAccessToken with no code_verifier yields an access token that Verifier.AccessToken accepts with the door's iss, the reset client's azp and the account's sub), and TC-992-35 (the start links reach the choose-user page).

column4: the runtime keycloak.conf option spi-password-policy--password-blacklist--false-positive-probability sets the false-positive probability of the Bloom filter passwordBlacklist checks the list through, under start --optimized with no rebuild; at the default 1.0E-4 the filter refuses about 1 in 10,000 unlisted passwords, at flows.DenylistFalsePositiveProbability (1e-9) none of 2,000,000, and every listed password is still refused (a Bloom filter has no false negatives)
